title: Anthropic: Redesigning source control at Anthropic (Scion)
summary: Anthropic built Scion, its own source control, when merges grew from 2,500 to over 30,000 a day: clients always online, a thin client and a server that answers every question, changesets as entries in a write-ahead log, everything content-addressed, derived data computed from parents, and no global locks.
ideas: Rethink priors made for human scale: ask what it would look like if designed for agents from the start.
A changeset records only what changed, as an entry in an append-only log; everything else is derived data, computed from its parents, eagerly or on demand.
Everything is content-addressed: stored once, never changed, cacheable anywhere without coordination.
One service answers every question about history through an API, so tools need no local copy.
Engineers review the intent of a change, not every line; their role is often to tell the agent no.
Adversarial review can be myopic: it pushes over-engineering in answer to hypothetical concerns.
Hermetic simulations of every interaction, and fuzzing, make the code well defended.
Superfans: an agent per component, watching its telemetry for anything strange.
No global lock on merging: test after merge and before deploy; agents fix conflicts fast.

took.idea: Records are append-only logs; stages and views are derived
One doc per thing, linked by path; nothing materialised twice
You review intent at Gate A; you say no to over-engineering
